signals.title: USD/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Fed Divergence
signals.text: The G10 scorecard shows USD leading peer currencies with an average gain of +1.208% across 9 pairs, while SEK anchors the laggard position at -0.968% across 2 pairs, generating a 2.176% bilateral spread. Fed policy rate sits at 4.00% with a hiking stance against the Riksbank on hold at 1.75%, delivering a +225bp nominal policy differential in favor of the dollar alongside a restrictive +1.59% US real policy rate versus -0.32% for Sweden. Economic surprise metrics reinforce the macroeconomic divergence, with the US ESI printing neutral at +2.2 while Sweden's ESI sinks to -29.2 amid persistent domestic data misses. USD/SEK trades at 9.826, tracking comfortably above its rising SMA20 (9.631), SMA50 (9.602), and SMA200 (9.357) stack. Although BEER fair-value modeling screens the pair rich at z=+1.79, widening yield advantages and the US bear-steepener backdrop sustain topside momentum. Trade bias: Bullish USD/SEK; macro outperformance and wide policy spread favor sustained upside. Catalyst: Riksbank policy decision 24 Sep — hold expected. Risk: Swedish data rebound and hawkish Riksbank guidance narrow the G10 bilateral spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Downside Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.07, holding above its SMA20 of 156.79 while remaining capped below the SMA50 at 159.05 and SMA200 at 158.40. The 287bp SOFR-TONA carry advantage (SOFR 3.85% vs TONA 0.98%) keeps structural dollar demand intact following recent rate increases from both the Fed to 4.00% and the BoJ to 1.25%. However, the options market exhibits pronounced downside hedging, with the 1M 25-delta risk reversal printing at -1.88, reflecting elevated put demand despite spot advancing +1.67% on the week. Concurrently, 1M ATM implied volatility sits at 8.0% against 30-day realized volatility of 9.9%, producing a negative volatility risk premium of -1.9% that signals underlying pricing vulnerability. Leveraged funds hold net long JPY positions of +20,069 contracts (95th percentile, z=+1.57), warning that speculative positioning has reached an upper-decile extreme even as spot struggles to reclaim moving-average resistance. Trade bias: Neutral/cautious USD/JPY; carry advantage is counterbalanced by heavy downside options hedging and stretched futures positioning. Catalyst: BoJ policy meeting 30 Oct. Risk: Spot closes above the SMA50 at 159.05, forcing option hedges to unwind and opening a grind toward the 160.00 intervention watch level.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Speculative Long
signals.text: CFTC data shows Leveraged Funds net long AUD at +59,299 contracts, positioning spec length at the 97th percentile of its 52-week distribution with a z-score of +2.11. Despite leveraged accounts adding +10,920 contracts WoW, spot has softened -0.44% over the past week to 0.7125. The pair trades below its descending SMA20 at 0.7168, though it remains supported above the SMA50 at 0.7087 and SMA200 at 0.7015. While a 50bp OIS carry premium favors the Aussie (AONIA 4.35% vs SOFR 3.85%), fresh geopolitical headwinds from US sanctions legislation and escalating tariff exposure toward China curb risk appetite. Options pricing corroborates upside exhaustion, with 1M 25-delta risk reversals leaning into a -0.66 put skew alongside a positive vol risk premium of +1.0% (IV 6.5% vs HV30 5.5%). Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD; crowded spec longs face liquidation risk as technical momentum stalls below short-term moving averages. Catalyst: RBA policy meeting 29 Sep — hold expected. Risk: A daily close above the SMA20 at 0.7168 signals fresh spec demand and invalidates the exhaustion read.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Bearish Moving-Average Breakdown
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1482, off -1.10% on the week and holding entirely below its primary moving-average cluster comprising the SMA20 at 1.1597, SMA50 at 1.1540, and SMA200 at 1.1633. The SOFR-€STR overnight differential of +141bp (SOFR 3.85% vs €STR 2.44%) reinforces underlying dollar dominance alongside the Fed's nominal policy rate of 4.00% versus the ECB's 2.65% deposit rate. Real policy rate differentials also penalize the euro, where the US real rate sits at +1.59% compared to the Eurozone's +0.30%. Leveraged positioning reflects moderate spec negativity with LF net short at -51,355 contracts, but the 32nd percentile reading (z=-0.36) leaves ample runway for further short accumulation. Options volatility remains subdued, with ATM IV at 4.5% versus HV30 at 4.2% (VRP +0.3%) and a near-flat risk reversal at -0.14, indicating little institutional appetite to fight the downward trend. Trade bias: Short EUR/USD; bearish technical trend aligned with carry and real yield disadvantage. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde speech 21 Sep at 11:00 UTC. Risk: Spot reclaims the SMA50 at 1.1540, signaling short-term trend stabilization.
